claim: Filopodia are thin, actin-based structures that cells use to interact with their environments.
source: Filopodia are thin, actin-based structures that cells use to interact with their environments.
evidence: This is a definitional statement about filopodia that draws from established scientific knowledge.

claim: Filopodia initiation requires a suite of conserved proteins.
source: Filopodia initiation requires a suite of conserved proteins but the mechanism remains poorly understood.
evidence: This statement is supported by established scientific consensus about filopodia formation.

claim: The actin polymerase VASP is essential for filopodia initiation.
source: The actin polymerase VASP and a MyTH-FERM (MF) myosin, DdMyo7 in amoeba, are essential for filopodia initiation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript showing that vasp null cells lack filopodia.

claim: DdMyo7 is essential for filopodia initiation in Dictyostelium.
source: The actin polymerase VASP and a MyTH-FERM (MF) myosin, DdMyo7 in amoeba, are essential for filopodia initiation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing that myo7 null cells lack filopodia.

claim: DdMyo7 is localized to dynamic regions of the actin-rich cortex.
source: DdMyo7 is localized to dynamic regions of the actin-rich cortex.
evidence: This claim is supported by microscopy data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Myosin recruitment and activation in Dictyostelium requires localized VASP-dependent actin polymerization.
source: Analysis of VASP mutants and treatment of cells with anti-actin drugs shows that myosin recruitment and activation in Dictyostelium requires localized VASP-dependent actin polymerization.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from VASP mutant analysis and drug treatment experiments.

claim: Targeting of DdMyo7 to the cortex alone is not sufficient for filopodia initiation.
source: Targeting of DdMyo7 to the cortex alone is not sufficient for filopodia initiation; VASP activity is also required.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing that DdMyo7-CAAX localized to the cortex in vasp null cells does not rescue filopodia formation.

claim: VASP activity is required for filopodia initiation even when DdMyo7 is targeted to the cortex.
source: Targeting of DdMyo7 to the cortex alone is not sufficient for filopodia initiation; VASP activity is also required.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from DdMyo7-CAAX expression in vasp null cells.

evidence: This claim is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

evidence: This claim is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

source: Although most intensely studied in animal cells, filopodia are ubiquitous in moving cells and have been observed in various Rhizaria, including predatory vampire amoebae, Discoba, Apusoza, Amoeboza, and Holozoa (Sebé-Pedrós et al., 2013; Cavalier-Smith and Chao, 2003; Hess et al., 2012; Hanousková et al., 2019; Yabuki et al., 2013).

source: Filopodia formation is orchestrated by a conserved core set of proteins that drive the formation and extension of actin bundles.
evidence: This claim is supported by established scientific knowledge and citations.

source: These include a Rho family GTPase (Rac1, Cdc42), an actin polymerase (VASP or formin), an actin cross-linker and a MyTH4-FERM Myosin (MF; myosin tail homology 4, band 4.1, ezrin, radixin, moesin) (Mattila and Lappalainen, 2008; Sebé-Pedrós et al., 2013; Nobes and Hall, 1995; Tuxworth et al., 2001; Faix et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

evidence: This claim is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: MF myosin motors regulate the formation of filopodia and other parallel actin based structures.
source: MF myosin motors regulate the formation of filopodia and other parallel actin based structures (Weck et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to other scholarly work.

claim: Dictyostelium amoebae null for DdMyo7 do not produce filopodia or any filopodia-like protrusions.
source: Dictyostelium amoebae null for DdMyo7 do not produce filopodia or any filopodia-like protrusions, and expression of Myo10 in various mammalian cell types induces filopodia formation, implicating these myosins in filopodia initiation (Bohil et al., 2006; Tuxworth et al., 2001; Sousa and Cheney, 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: Expression of Myo10 in various mammalian cell types induces filopodia formation.
source: Dictyostelium amoebae null for DdMyo7 do not produce filopodia or any filopodia-like protrusions, and expression of Myo10 in various mammalian cell types induces filopodia formation, implicating these myosins in filopodia initiation (Bohil et al., 2006; Tuxworth et al., 2001; Sousa and Cheney, 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: MF myosins are strikingly localized to filopodia tips.
source: These MF myosins are strikingly localized to filopodia tips, yet their function during filopodia initiation remains poorly defined.
evidence: This claim is supported by established scientific knowledge and observations.

claim: Filopodia are slender, actin-filled projections that extend from the cell cortex.
source: Filopodia are slender, actin-filled projections that extend from the cell cortex.
evidence: This is a definitional statement about filopodia that draws from established scientific knowledge.

claim: Actin polymerization aided by VASP or formin facilitates the formation of a critical bundle size of 15–20 filaments which overcomes membrane tension and extends outwards as the actin filaments are cross-linked together.
source: Actin polymerization aided by VASP or formin facilitates the formation of a critical bundle size of 15–20 filaments which overcomes membrane tension and extends outwards as the actin filaments are cross-linked together (Mattila and Lappalainen, 2008; Mogilner and Rubinstein, 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: In one model, the branched actin network is reorganized into a parallel array by the polymerase and bundler VASP.
source: In one case, the branched actin network is reorganized into a parallel array by the polymerase and bundler VASP (Svitkina et al., 2003; Yang and Svitkina, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: In an alternative model, a linear actin polymerase such as formin nucleates new filaments that are rapidly bundled together and grow perpendicular to the plasma membrane.
source: In an alternative model, a linear actin polymerase such as formin nucleates new filaments that are rapidly bundled together and grow perpendicular to the plasma membrane (Faix and Rottner, 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to other scholarly work.

claim: MF myosins are thought to act during initiation by cross-linking actin filaments.
source: MF myosins are thought to act during initiation by cross-linking actin filaments (Tokuo et al., 2007), perhaps zipping them together as the motors walk up the filament toward the cortex (Berg and Cheney, 2002; Ropars et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: Forced dimers of motors can induce filopodia or filopodia-like protrusions in cells.
source: Support for this model comes from the observation that forced dimers of motors can induce filopodia or filopodia-like protrusions in cells (Tokuo et al., 2007; Arthur et al., 2019; Masters and Buss, 2017; Liu et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: Myo10 has been implicated in elongation by transporting VASP toward the tip of the growing filopodium to promote continued growth.
source: Myo10 has also been implicated in elongation by transporting VASP toward the tip of the growing filopodium to promote continued growth (Tokuo and Ikebe, 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to other scholarly work.

claim: MF myosins are regulated by head-tail autoinhibition, with the myosin folded into a compact conformation whereby binding of the C-terminal MF domain to the motor domain inhibits its activity.
source: These myosins are regulated by head-tail autoinhibition, with the myosin folded into a compact conformation whereby binding of the C-terminal MF domain to the motor domain inhibits its activity.
evidence: This claim is supported by established scientific knowledge and citations.

claim: Opening up of the myosin followed by dimerization is required for activation of the myosin.
source: Opening up of the myosin followed by dimerization is required for activation of the myosin (Umeki et al., 2011; Sakai et al., 2011; Yang et al., 2006; Arthur et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: Partner binding mediated by MF domains can typically stabilize the open, activated form of these myosins as well as promote dimerization.
source: Partner binding mediated by their MyTH4-FERM (MF) domains can typically stabilize the open, activated form of these myosins as well as promote dimerization (Sakai et al., 2011; Arthur et al., 2019; Liu et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: The MF domains in these myosins can mediate interaction with partner proteins such as microtubules.
source: The MF domains in these myosins can indeed mediate interaction with partner proteins such as microtubules (Weber et al., 2004; Toyoshima and Nishida, 2007; Planelles-Herrero et al., 2016) and the cytoplasmic tails of adhesion and signaling receptors (Hirao et al., 1996; Hamada et al., 2000; Zhang et al., 2004; Zhu et al., 2007; Pi et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: The MF domains in these myosins can mediate interaction with the cytoplasmic tails of adhesion and signaling receptors.
source: The MF domains in these myosins can indeed mediate interaction with partner proteins such as microtubules (Weber et al., 2004; Toyoshima and Nishida, 2007; Planelles-Herrero et al., 2016) and the cytoplasmic tails of adhesion and signaling receptors (Hirao et al., 1996; Hamada et al., 2000; Zhang et al., 2004; Zhu et al., 2007; Pi et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: Myo10 has a unique tail among MF myosins with PH domains that bind to PIP3 rich membranes, which facilitates autoinhibition release and subsequent dimerization via a coiled-coil domain.
source: Myo10 has a unique tail among MF myosins with PH domains that bind to PIP3 rich membranes, which facilitates autoinhibition release and subsequent dimerization via a coiled-coil domain (Plantard et al., 2010; Umeki et al., 2011; Lu et al., 2012; Ropars et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: DdMyo7, like mammalian microvilli and stereocilia myosins Myo7 and Myo15, lacks PH domains.
source: DdMyo7, like mammalian microvilli and stereocilia myosins Myo7 and Myo15, lacks PH domains and it is not clear if activation is regulated by the concentration of some partners, or additional cellular signals.
evidence: This claim is supported by established scientific knowledge.

claim: MF myosin and the actin regulators VASP and formin have been observed to coalesce into punctae during the initiation step that precedes extension.
source: MF myosin and the actin regulators VASP and formin have been observed to coalesce into punctae during the initiation step that precedes extension (Petersen et al., 2016; Young et al., 2018; Cheng and Mullins, 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: Disruption of the Dictyostelium myoi (myo7) gene encoding DdMyo7 results in a significant defect in filopodia formation.
source: Disruption of the Dictyostelium myoi (myo7) gene encoding DdMyo7 results in a significant defect in filopodia formation that is rescued by expression of GFP-DdMyo7 (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplements 1A and 2A; Tuxworth et al., 2001; Petersen et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures and cited references.

claim: The filopodia formation defect in myo7 null cells is rescued by expression of GFP-DdMyo7.
source: Disruption of the Dictyostelium myoi (myo7) gene encoding DdMyo7 results in a significant defect in filopodia formation that is rescued by expression of GFP-DdMyo7 (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplements 1A and 2A; Tuxworth et al., 2001; Petersen et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures and cited references.

claim: DdMyo7 is most strikingly localized to filopodia tips.
source: Most strikingly localized to filopodia tips, DdMyo7 is also in the cytosol and localized to the leading edge of cells (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by microscopy data shown in figures.

claim: DdMyo7 is also in the cytosol and localized to the leading edge of cells.
source: Most strikingly localized to filopodia tips, DdMyo7 is also in the cytosol and localized to the leading edge of cells (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by microscopy data shown in figures.

claim: The tail domain (aa 809 - end) of DdMyo7 is localized all around the cell periphery in contrast to the full-length myosin which is often restricted at one edge of the cell cortex.
source: In the course of characterizing functionally important regions of DdMyo7, it was observed that the tail domain (aa 809 - end) is localized all around the cell periphery in contrast to the full-length myosin which is often restricted at one edge of the cell cortex, (Figure 1B; Petersen et al., 2016; Arthur et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by microscopy data shown in figures and cited references.

claim: There is less correlation between DdMyo7 and the tail (r = 0.63) than is seen for the two full-length myosins (r = 0.86).
source: Quantification revealed less correlation between DdMyo7 and the tail (r = 0.63) than is seen for the two full-length myosins (r = 0.86) (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis of microscopy data shown in figures.

claim: Actin is typically enriched at the leading edge with high intensity at one edge and lower intensity elsewhere.
source: Actin is typically enriched at the leading edge with high intensity at one edge and lower intensity elsewhere (Figure 1F,G).
evidence: This claim is supported by microscopy data shown in figures.

claim: Actin (RFP-Lifeact) and GFP-DdMyo7 are localized asymmetrically with a high standard deviation of cortical intensity.
source: This analysis shows that actin (RFP-Lifeact; Brzeska et al., 2014) and GFP-DdMyo7 are localized asymmetrically with a high standard deviation of cortical intensity (Figure 1F,G,I).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis of microscopy data shown in figures.

claim: The tail appears uniformly localized around the periphery and has a lower average SD for the cortical intensity around the cell periphery.
source: In contrast, the tail appears uniformly localized around the periphery (Figure 1F,G) and has a lower average SD for the cortical intensity around the cell periphery (Figure 1I).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis of microscopy data shown in figures.

claim: A tail-less forced dimer of the motor (motor-FD) that is capable of inducing filopodial protrusions is also localized asymmetrically with a high standard deviation of intensity.
source: Interestingly, a tail-less forced dimer of the motor (motor-FD; Figure 1A) that is capable of inducing filopodial protrusions (Arthur et al., 2019) is also localized asymmetrically with a high standard deviation of intensity (Figure 1F,I).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis of microscopy data shown in figures and cited references.

claim: Restricted localization of full-length DdMyo7 is dependent on its motor domain.
source: Together, these data establish that restricted localization of full-length DdMyo7 is dependent on its motor domain.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data comparing full-length DdMyo7, tail, and motor-FD localization.

claim: DdMyo7 and actin appear to colocalize at the leading edge in cells expressing both GFP-DdMyo7 and an actin marker (Lifeact).
source: DdMyo7 and actin appear to colocalize at the leading edge in cells expressing both GFP-DdMyo7 and an actin marker (Lifeact) (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by microscopy data shown in figures.

claim: There is strong correlation of Lifeact and DdMyo7 fluorescence around the cell periphery.
source: Linescans show that indeed there is strong correlation of Lifeact and DdMyo7 fluorescence around the cell periphery (Figure 2B, yellow line from 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis of microscopy data shown in figures.

claim: Cytofluorogram analysis revealed strong correlation of the DdMyo7 and actin fluorescence intensities.
source: Cytofluorogram analysis also revealed strong correlation of the DdMyo7 and actin fluorescence intensities (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis of microscopy data shown in figures.

claim: A line scan taken perpendicular to an extending leading edge showed a steady accumulation of DdMyo7 intensity at the same time as an increase in actin intensity.
source: A line scan taken perpendicular to an extending leading edge showed a steady accumulation of DdMyo7 intensity at the same time as an increase in actin intensity (Figure 2D,E).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis of microscopy data shown in figures.

claim: DdMyo7 and actin normalized intensities during leading edge extension show a robust correlation with actin intensity.
source: DdMyo7 and actin normalized intensities during leading edge extension were measured for 10 independent cells and a spline fit shows a robust correlation with actin intensity (Figure 2F).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis of microscopy data shown in figures.

claim: CytochalasinA (cytoA) binds to the fast-growing (barbed) end of actin filaments and blocks incorporation of actin monomers, capping and stabilizing filaments.
source: CytochalasinA (cytoA) binds to the fast-growing (barbed) end of actin filaments and blocks incorporation of actin monomers, capping and stabilizing filaments (Cooper, 1987).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to other scholarly work.

claim: LatrunculinA (latA) sequesters monomers and prevents actin filament growth.
source: LatrunculinA (latA) sequesters monomers and prevents actin filament growth, and CK-666 blocks the Arp2/3 complex and actin branching (Coué et al., 1987; Nolen et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: CK-666 blocks the Arp2/3 complex and actin branching.
source: LatrunculinA (latA) sequesters monomers and prevents actin filament growth, and CK-666 blocks the Arp2/3 complex and actin branching (Coué et al., 1987; Nolen et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: Control cells have a cortex:cytoplasm ratio of about ~1.2, indicating an overall 20% enrichment of DdMyo7 on the cell cortex.
source: Control cells have a cortex:cytoplasm ratio of about ~1.2, indicating an overall 20% enrichment of DdMyo7 on the cell cortex (Figure 2G,H; Arthur et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis of microscopy data shown in figures and cited references.

claim: Treatment of cells with either cytoA or latA reduced the ratio to ~1 indicating a total loss of cortical localization of DdMyo7.
source: Treatment of cells with either cytoA or latA reduced the ratio to ~1 indicating a total loss of cortical localization of DdMyo7 (Figure 2H).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis of microscopy data shown in figures.

claim: CK-666 significantly reduced DdMyo7 cortical recruitment.
source: CK-666 also significantly reduced DdMyo7 cortical recruitment (Figure 2G,H).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis of microscopy data shown in figures.

claim: Filopodia formation was significantly reduced with actin modulating drugs cytoA, latA, and CK-666.
source: Consistent with the reduction or loss of polymerized actin and cortical DdMyo7, filopodia formation was significantly reduced with these actin modulating drugs (Table 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data shown in tables.

claim: Jasplakinolide (jasp) promotes monomer nucleation and stabilizes ADP-Pi actin filaments.
source: Cells were also treated with jasplakinolide (jasp) that promotes monomer nucleation and stabilizes ADP-Pi actin filaments (Merino et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to other scholarly work.

claim: Jasp treatment resulted in increased recruitment of DdMyo7 to the cortex and increased filopodia formation.
source: Jasp treatment had the opposite effect, resulting in increased recruitment of DdMyo7 to the cortex and increased filopodia formation (Figure 2G,H; Table 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis of microscopy data shown in figures and tables.

claim: The addition of PI3Kinase inhibitors did not disrupt DdMyo7 cortical targeting or filopodia formation.
source: The addition of PI3Kinase inhibitors did not disrupt DdMyo7 cortical targeting or filopodia formation, but did disrupt the localization of a PIP3 reporter (GFP-CRAC, Parent et al., 1998; Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–C, Table 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis of microscopy data shown in figures and tables.

claim: PI3Kinase inhibitors disrupted the localization of a PIP3 reporter (GFP-CRAC).
source: The addition of PI3Kinase inhibitors did not disrupt DdMyo7 cortical targeting or filopodia formation, but did disrupt the localization of a PIP3 reporter (GFP-CRAC, Parent et al., 1998; Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–C, Table 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis of microscopy data shown in figures and tables.

claim: Microtubules have been implicated in regulating filopodia in melanoma cells, modulating their localization, density and merging.
source: Microtubules have been implicated in regulating filopodia in melanoma cells, modulating their localization, density and merging (Schober et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to other scholarly work.

claim: Treatment of Dictyostelium cells with the microtubule depolymerizing compound nocodazole disrupts cytosolic microtubules.
source: Treatment of Dictyostelium cells with the microtubule depolymerizing compound nocodazole disrupts cytosolic microtubules (visualized by cells expressing GFP-tubulin Neujahr et al., 1998, Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by microscopy data shown in figures and cited references.

claim: Nocodazole reduced DdMyo7 cortical targeting and partially inhibited filopodia formation, particularly at higher concentrations (50 µM).
source: Nocodazole reduced DdMyo7 cortical targeting and partially inhibited filopodia formation, particularly at higher concentrations (50 µM) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E,G,I; Table 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis of microscopy data shown in figures and tables.

claim: Cortical targeting of the DdMyo7 tail fragment is not reduced in cells treated with nocodazole.
source: Interestingly, cortical targeting of the DdMyo7 tail fragment is not reduced in cells treated with nocodazole (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F,H) in spite of the presence of two MF domains with micromolar affinity for microtubules in the DdMyo7 tail (Planelles-Herrero et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis of microscopy data shown in figures and cited references.

claim: DdMyo7 tail has two MF domains with micromolar affinity for microtubules.
source: Interestingly, cortical targeting of the DdMyo7 tail fragment is not reduced in cells treated with nocodazole (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F,H) in spite of the presence of two MF domains with micromolar affinity for microtubules in the DdMyo7 tail (Planelles-Herrero et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to other scholarly work.

claim: DdMyo7 is not strongly localized to microtubules.
source: Additionally, DdMyo7 is not strongly localized to microtubules (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D,E).
evidence: This claim is supported by microscopy data shown in figures.

claim: Microtubule-actin crosstalk may impact the dynamics of the cortical actin network and thus indirectly control the cortical recruitment of full-length DdMyo7.
source: Together, the data suggest that microtubule-actin crosstalk may impact the dynamics of the cortical actin network and thus indirectly control the cortical recruitment of full-length DdMyo7.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data on nocodazole treatment effects.

claim: Dictyostelium VASP is a potent actin polymerase.
source: Dictyostelium VASP is a potent actin polymerase, its activity speeds actin elongation, bundles filaments and blocks capping proteins from binding to the growing ends of actin filaments (Breitsprecher et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to other scholarly work.

claim: VASP activity speeds actin elongation, bundles filaments and blocks capping proteins from binding to the growing ends of actin filaments.
source: Dictyostelium VASP is a potent actin polymerase, its activity speeds actin elongation, bundles filaments and blocks capping proteins from binding to the growing ends of actin filaments (Breitsprecher et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to other scholarly work.

claim: Both VASP's actin polymerization and bundling activities could be important for DdMyo7 recruitment.
source: Both its actin polymerization and bundling activities could be important for DdMyo7 recruitment (Figure 5).
evidence: This claim is inferred from experimental data shown in figures.

claim: In the absence of DdVASP, increased cortical actin generated by the formin dDia2 can also recruit and activate DdMyo7.
source: In the absence of DdVASP, increased cortical actin generated by the formin dDia2 can also recruit and activate DdMyo7 (Figure 4B-E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: Recruitment of DdMyo7 is not restored by generating actin waves, polymerizing actin with jasplakinolide or blocking capping protein by overexpression of V-1 in vasp null cells.
source: However, recruitment is not restored by several other means of increasing actin polymerization, including generating actin waves, polymerizing actin with jasplakinolide or blocking capping protein by overexpression of V-1.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: DdVASP does not simply recruit DdMyo7 by generating new actin polymers, but rather it is the nature of the network that DdVASP builds, likely growing linear actin filaments that are bundled together in parallel, that is critical for activation of DdMyo7.
source: Thus, DdVASP does not simply recruit DdMyo7 by generating new actin polymers, but rather it is the nature of the network that DdVASP builds, likely growing linear actin filaments that are bundled together in parallel, that is critical for activation of DdMyo7.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data comparing different methods of actin polymerization.

claim: The actin cortex of vasp nulls is less dense than found for wild-type cells as revealed by phalloidin staining.
source: The actin cortex of vasp nulls is less dense than found for wild-type cells as revealed by phalloidin staining, suggesting that a robust leading edge actin network collapses without VASP (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by microscopy data shown in figures.

claim: A robust leading edge actin network collapses without VASP.
source: The actin cortex of vasp nulls is less dense than found for wild-type cells as revealed by phalloidin staining, suggesting that a robust leading edge actin network collapses without VASP (Figure 4D).
